title: Fast internet isn't just speed: latency vs bandwidth explained
description: Bandwidth is how much data fits through, and latency is how long it takes to arrive. Gamers and video callers feel the difference.

scenes.sub: and most people only check one
scenes.say: Internet speed isn't one number. It's two. And a speed test only checks one of them.
Bandwidth is capacity, the maximum data at once. Latency is time, how long one piece takes to get there. A wide pipe can still be a long one.

Ping measures latency. Distance matters most. Cloudflare says users around a hundred miles from a server see roughly five to ten milliseconds, but around twenty-two hundred miles away, forty to fifty.
Several things add delay. Distance, the number of networks crossed, equipment on the path, and even using Wi-Fi instead of Ethernet.

scenes.sub: bandwidth for streams, latency for games
scenes.say: So streaming loves bandwidth, but games and video calls care far more about latency. Next time your connection feels slow, ask which one is the problem. Follow for more networking basics, explained simply.
